title: Iniesta 2010 World Cup Final — Spain 1-0 Netherlands, 116th minute
body: 11 July 2010, Soccer City Stadium, Johannesburg. The 2010 FIFA World Cup Final between Spain and the Netherlands. Spain had never won a World Cup in their 76-year footballing history. The match was tense, brutal, and marred by 14 yellow cards (a Final record). Nigel de Jong's flying kick to Xabi Alonso's chest in the first half summed up the tone. Through 90 minutes and into extra time, the score was 0-0. In the 116th minute, with penalties looming, Cesc Fabregas — on as a substitute — slipped a first-time pass through the Dutch defence. Andres Iniesta, the slightly-built Barcelona midfielder, ran on to it. Stekelenburg, the Dutch keeper, came rushing out. Iniesta took the ball on his chest, let it drop, and volleyed it half-volley past Stekelenburg into the bottom-right corner of the net. Spain 1-0 Netherlands. Cesc Fabregas mobbed him. Iniesta lifted his Spain shirt to reveal a hand-written message: 'Dani Jarque siempre con nosotros' — Dani Jarque always with us — a tribute to his Espanyol friend who had died of a heart attack the year before. Cards: Iniesta was booked for removing his shirt. Spain became World Champions for the first time in their history. The Spanish commentator Manuel Lama on Cuatro screamed 'GOOOOOOL DE ESPAÑA, GOOOOOOL DE INIESTA!' — joined by tears.
